claims.statement: The Extraction Guide describes a fast, under-extracted shot as tasting 'bitter/sharp, weak and watery' and an over-extracted shot as 'bitter and burnt'; only the summary table links under-extraction to 'sour'.
A Lemmy owner said they had first misjudged sour as bitter, and that grinding finer made the shot even more sour.
On the Barista Express the target shot time is 25–30 s, under 20 s is under-extracted, and the 2-cup dose is 16–19 g.
The Barista Express gauge zones are Under, Within and Over Espresso Range, with no bar values given.
The Barista Express booklet gives two different flow-start figures: 4–7 s and 8–12 s.
The Barista Pro has no pressure gauge; its LCD shot clock counts up from the start of the shot.
On the Barista Pro, flow starting at 8–12 s is right, before 7 s is under-extracted, and no flow after 13 s is over-extracted.
Dual-wall baskets regulate the pressure regardless of grind, dose, tamp or freshness; single-wall baskets are for fresh whole beans.
The Barista Pro ships with the single-wall 2-cup basket installed.
The Barista Express GRIND AMOUNT dial starts at 3 o'clock and is adjusted until the tamper's metal cap is level with the basket rim after tamping.
The Barista Pro GRIND AMOUNT sets grind time, with defaults of 9.5 s (single) and 13 s (double), and the dose is checked by the tamper-cap level.
A finer grind in single-wall baskets may need a larger grind amount, because dosing depends on how long the grinder runs.
1 CUP and 2 CUP stop at a preset volume of about 30 ml or 60 ml, and the cup output varies with grind size and grind amount; a manual shot is press and hold, release, press to stop.
On the Barista Express, setting 1 is finest and 16 coarsest; on the Barista Pro, 1 is finest, 30 coarsest and 15 is the default.
Grind should be fine but not too fine, and the factors should be adjusted one at a time.
The upper (inner) burr is a documented owner adjustment on both machines, moved one number at a time using its wire handle after emptying the hopper and running the grinder empty.
Beans should have a Roasted On date and be used 5–20 days after roasting; stale coffee may pour too quickly and taste bitter and watery.

A cold portafilter and basket can reduce extraction temperature enough to significantly affect quality; the basket should be wiped dry because moisture encourages channeling; a short flow through the group stabilises temperature.
Barista Express Advanced Temperature Mode (power off, hold PROGRAM, press POWER) adjusts brew temperature up to 4°F either way in 2°F steps.
Holding PROGRAM until three beeps resets the default shot volumes and the default espresso water temperature.
Barista Pro shot temperature is set in the SHOT TEMP menu, with no stated range.
The troubleshooting tables list a coarse grind, not enough coffee and a light tamp as the causes of espresso running out too quickly.
The only troubleshooting row that sends owners to support is the thermal cut-out; fast shots and no crema are attributed to grind, dose, tamp, freshness, a blocked basket and basket choice.
Mineral build-up is linked to reduced brewing flow and to espresso dripping or not flowing, not to fast shots.
A new Express owner thought the gauge was broken; it moved after grinding at 1–2, filling the basket higher and tamping harder, and they kept the machine.
Over-extracted shots are fixed with a coarser grind and a smaller grind amount; over 35 s is over-extracted on the Express.
